summary: WebSocket ping/pong race leads to truncated terminal fragments and out-of-order resume after reconnect
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated partial terminations of WebSocket streaming sessions where the final fragment (closing JSON envelope) is truncated during a short-lived network disturbance. After reconnect, resume attempts deliver duplicated metadata messages and the final 'end' marker sometimes arrives out of order or not at all. Impact: Affected customer workflows that post-process streamed tokens (markdown rendering and attachment extraction) observe corrupted output and missing attachments for ~3-8% of long streaming sessions (document generation flow).
impact: Loss/mangling of final tokens and trailing attachments in streamed responses; downstream parser fails producing invalid markdown and missing embedded image URLs; customer pipeline retries leading to duplicated records.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer opens a WebSocket streaming session to /v1/stream with model=redwood-vicuna-1.3, streaming=true and a large prompt (approx 1.5k tokens output expected).
2) During streaming, induce a brief path-change by simulating an edge NAT churn or TCP connection preemption (reproduce in lab with lb connection drain).
3) Client performs a reconnect and attempts resume using last_seen_token_id in resume header.
4) Observe final fragments: terminal envelope either lost, truncated JSON, or duplicated metadata events and embedded image URL missing from final payload.
observed_behavior: Terminal JSON envelope is truncated (partial last chunk) or arrives after a duplicate metadata block. Resume sequence numbers sometimes decrease on server side causing out-of-order finalization events to be emitted to the client. WS ping/pong exchange recorded within 50-150ms of the disconnect is correlated with the truncated payloads.
expected_behavior: On short reconnects, resume should stitch stream fragments deterministically: no duplication of metadata, final 'end' envelope sent once and in-order, and attachments preserved intact.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Ping/pong race combined with connection handoff leads to duplicate resume processing path in gateway causing a partial flush in worker output buffer.
Reproduced in staging with lb drain + synthetic 100-200ms pong delays. Failure rate ~4% for long outputs (>1k tokens).

Tracing shows two resume events for same stream_id hitting different worker processes (wr-11 and wr-12) within 30ms window; both emit metadata, only one writes end envelope but its final write was interrupted by socket swap, causing truncated bytes on wire.

Socket swap sequence: old socket close triggers soft-close that still delivers partial buffered bytes; new socket resume also pushes metadata — client sees duplicate metadata and either truncated final JSON or final marker after duplicate metadata.
temporary_workaround: Customer can set client-side logic to wait for a deterministic final 'end' marker and re-request missing attachments via the REST attachments endpoint if end marker not observed within X seconds. Also lowering client ping frequency to avoid near-simultaneous ping/pong during handoffs helped reduce incidence in staging.
proposed_fix: 1) Gate resume processing in gateway so only one resume token is accepted per stream_id (atomic compare-and-set). 2) Ensure worker final writes are flushed to stable socket before acknowledging resume success; add end-marker ack from gateway to worker to prevent duplicate resume. 3) Add a short dedupe window for metadata events before forwarding to client.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to prototype atomic resume acceptor in gateway (owner: Samir).
2) Add end-marker ack and test flush semantics in runtime (owner: runtime team).
3) Run 48h staging soak with synthetic handoffs and large outputs; target <0.1% failure rate.
4) Communicate interim mitigation to customer support and update runbook for reconnect scenarios.

root_cause: Race condition: gateway allowed multiple concurrent resume acceptances during socket swap; worker final write could be interrupted by soft-close leaving truncated payload on wire.
actions_taken: Added staging detection rule for duplicate resume events; provided customer guidance and REST fallback for attachments. PR opened to fix gating and flush semantics.
